edges.label: hypothesis: could be worth testing
edges.explanation: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. The atlas computed this chain: VAMP2-related disorders is linked to Protein destabilization / misfolding by a driven_by edge, and 4-Phenylbutyrate / glycerol phenylbutyrate (chemical chaperone) is aimed at that same mechanism; and the graph has no developed_for edge and no study testing this therapy class in this disease. The weakest link is the VAMP2 destabilization edge itself: it is a contested edge resting on one 2025 paper, and that paper's 'stability' defect is a SNARE-complex property, not the degradation-and-rescue event that 4-PBA is known to act on. Nobody has tested this.

Published work links VAMP2-related disorders to protein destabilization / misfolding. Nine variants differing in SNARE-complex affinity, stability and conformation. Contradicting or limiting findings are attached as counter-evidence: Some VAMP2 variants augment spontaneous release rather than only i

counter_evidence.title: 4-Phenylbutyrate restored γ-aminobutyric acid uptake and reduced seizures in SLC6A1 patient variant-bearing cell and mouse models.
counter_evidence.quote: Although the mechanisms of action for 4-phenylbutyrate are still unclear, with multiple possibly being involved, it is likely that 4-phenylbutyrate can facilitate the forward trafficking of the wildtype γ-amino butyric acid transporter 1 regardless of rescuing the mutant γ-amino butyric acid transporter 1, thus increasing γ-amino butyric acid uptake.

counter_evidence.title: Synaptobrevin-2 disease variants reveal spatial constraints within the presynaptic active zone.
counter_evidence.quote: The neurotransmission deficits we observed parallel the symptomatic heterogeneity of the patients, with some variants displaying a disproportionate augmentation of spontaneous neurotransmitter release.

attrs.title: 4-phenylbutyrate for VAMP2-related disorders
attrs.weakest_link: the VAMP2 destabilization edge itself: it is a contested edge resting on one 2025 paper, and that paper's 'stability' defect is a SNARE-complex property, not the degradation-and-rescue event that 4-PBA is known to act on.

caveats.text: Only 7 of 35 pathogenic VAMP2 records in ClinVar are missense; a chaperone has nothing to stabilise in a truncating or whole-gene-deletion case.
The VAMP2 'stability' finding is a biophysical and neuronal characterisation of nine variants, not a patient result.

caveats.kind: mechanism may not be the same kind of instability
caveats.text: Synaptobrevin-2 is natively unstructured outside the SNARE complex, so 'destabilization' here is not the folded-protein-degraded case that chemical chaperones were developed for.
4-phenylbutyrate's own mechanism is unresolved: in SLC6A1 models it may act on wild-type trafficking rather than on the mutant protein, and the generic chaperones need high concentrations.
Some VAMP2 variants increase spontaneous release rather than reduce fusion; raising the amount of such a protein is not obviously good.

caveat_citations.title: Synaptobrevin-2 disease variants reveal spatial constraints within the presynaptic active zone.
caveat_citations.quote: Here, we investigated nine synaptobrevin-2 (VAMP2) disease-causing variants and uncovered their specific SNARE complex affinity, stability, and conformational deficits that drive dysregulated neurotransmission.

caveat_citations.title: Oligomerisation of Synaptobrevin-2 Studied by Native Mass Spectrometry and Chemical Cross-Linking.
caveat_citations.quote: While Synaptobrevin-2 is part of a four-helix bundle in this SNARE complex, it is natively unstructured in the absence of lipids or other SNARE proteins.

caveat_citations.title: 4-Phenylbutyrate restored γ-aminobutyric acid uptake and reduced seizures in SLC6A1 patient variant-bearing cell and mouse models.
caveat_citations.quote: Although the mechanisms of action for 4-phenylbutyrate are still unclear, with multiple possibly being involved, it is likely that 4-phenylbutyrate can facilitate the forward trafficking of the wildtype γ-amino butyric acid transporter 1 regardless of rescuing the mutant γ-amino butyric acid transporter 1, thus increasing γ-amino butyric acid uptake.

caveat_citations.title: Targeted stabilization of Munc18-1 function via pharmacological chaperones.
caveat_citations.quote: No disease-modifying therapy exists to treat these disorders, and while chemical chaperones have been shown to alleviate neuronal dysfunction caused by missense mutations in Munc18-1, their required high concentrations and potential toxicity necessitate a Munc18-1-targeted therapy.

caveat_citations.title: Synaptobrevin-2 disease variants reveal spatial constraints within the presynaptic active zone.
caveat_citations.quote: The neurotransmission deficits we observed parallel the symptomatic heterogeneity of the patients, with some variants displaying a disproportionate augmentation of spontaneous neurotransmitter release.

test.what_to_test: In a VAMP2-variant neuronal model, measure variant protein level, SNARE-complex formation and evoked/spontaneous release with and without 4-phenylbutyrate, variant by variant - starting with the C-terminal SNARE-motif variants that were characterised as destabilised, and including one variant that augments spontaneous release as a negative control.
test.existing_assay_note: The readouts already exist on both sides: the Munc18-1 chaperone work (PMID:30266908) established the rescue assay, and the VAMP2 variant panel (PMID:41166419) established the electrophysiology. The MRC UCL-Yale VAMP2 project is the group with the reagents; Simons Searchlight covers VAMP2 patients.
test.what_result_would_change_the_plan: If 4-PBA raises variant VAMP2 protein and restores evoked release without increasing spontaneous release, VAMP2 becomes a candidate arm on the existing phenylbutyrate protocol. If it only raises wild-type protein, or if it increases spontaneous release, the hypothesis dies and the STXBP1/SLC6A1 bridge stays a two-gene story.

edges.label: hypothesis: could be worth testing
edges.explanation: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding. The atlas computed this chain: the gene participates in Ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis and 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) is aimed at that process (no edge says this disease dysregulates it in the direction the drug pushes); and the graph has no developed_for edge and no study testing this therapy class in this disease. The weakest link is the pathway chain plus the contested mechanism: STXBP1 reaches this drug class only through 'the gene participates in Ca2+-triggered exocytosis', while the direction of its own release defect is disputed in the literature. Nobody has tested this.

evidence.title: 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) is aimed at ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis.
Variants in STXBP1 cause STXBP1-related disorders. Curated databases record 1 clinical entity under this umbrella; gene-disease validity is definitive in Gene2Phenotype and definitive in ClinGen.
Gene Ontology annotates STXBP1 to ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis (GO:0048791 or a more specific child term), evidence codes IBA.

attrs.title: Aminopyridines for STXBP1 variants that reduce release
attrs.weakest_link: the pathway chain plus the contested mechanism: STXBP1 reaches this drug class only through 'the gene participates in Ca2+-triggered exocytosis', while the direction of its own release defect is disputed in the literature.

caveats.text: A homozygous STXBP1 variant (L446F) causes a gain-of-function phenotype for release probability, the opposite of the group a release-boosting drug would help.
Every STXBP1 mechanism edge in the graph is contested: haploinsufficiency, destabilization and dominant-negative all carry counter-evidence.
No neuromuscular presentation is recorded for STXBP1, and the drug's clinical evidence base is neuromuscular.
Reduced release in STXBP1 comes with depleted interacting proteins (syntaxin-1, Doc2), so pushing the remaining machinery harder may not be equivalent to restoring it.

caveat_citations.title: Analysis of conditional heterozygous STXBP1 mutations in human neurons.
caveat_citations.quote: We demonstrated that heterozygous STXBP1 mutations lower the levels of Munc18-1 protein and its binding partner, the t-SNARE-protein Syntaxin-1, by approximately 30% and decrease spontaneous and evoked neurotransmitter release by nearly 50%.

caveat_citations.title: Disease-linked mutations in Munc18-1 deplete synaptic Doc2.
caveat_citations.quote: Using biochemical and cell biological readouts on mouse brains, cultured mouse neurons and heterologous cells, we found that the synaptic Munc18-1 interactors Doc2A and Doc2B are unstable in the absence of Munc18-1 and aggregate in the presence of disease-causing Munc18-1 mutants.

test.what_to_test: In Stxbp1+/- neurons and in patient iPSC neurons, test whether 4-aminopyridine restores evoked release, and whether it does so without increasing spontaneous release or network hyperexcitability.
test.existing_assay_note: STXBP1 is the only disease in the slice with model assets and an outcome-measure consortium, so this is the cheapest of these experiments to run.
test.what_result_would_change_the_plan: Network hyperexcitability in the model would end it immediately. A clean rescue would make a variant-stratified pilot arguable - but only alongside the existing anti-seizure regimen, never instead.

evidence.title: 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) is aimed at ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis.
Variants in STX1B cause STX1B-related epilepsies. Curated databases record 2 clinical entities under this umbrella; gene-disease validity is strong in Gene2Phenotype and definitive in ClinGen.
Gene Ontology annotates STX1B to ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis (GO:0048791 or a more specific child term), evidence codes IEA.

attrs.title: Aminopyridines for the loss-of-function end of STX1B epilepsy
attrs.weakest_link: the direction of effect: the gene's own variants point both ways, so a gene-level hypothesis is unsafe and only a variant-level one survives.

caveats.text: STX1B contains variants that reduce the releasable pool AND variants that increase fusogenicity, and patient iPSC neurons show one variant doing both.
The STX1B loss-of-function edge is contested in the graph, and one cohort found loss-of-function variants in very differently affected people.
This is an epilepsy population and the drug class has a dose-related seizure risk.
No neuromuscular presentation is recorded for STX1B, so the NMJ evidence behind this drug class does not carry over.

caveat_citations.title: Epilepsy-causing STX1B mutations translate altered protein functions into distinct phenotypes in mouse neurons.
caveat_citations.quote: The mutation STX1BV216E, also causing epileptic encephalopathies, only slightly diminishes Munc18-1 and Munc13 interactions, but leads to enhanced fusogenicity and increased vesicular release probability, also in STX1-null neurons.

caveat_citations.title: STX1B variant-specific synaptic dysfunction is associated with network hyperexcitability in human iPSC-derived neurons.
caveat_citations.quote: FINDINGS: G226R exhibited both gain- and loss-of-function characteristics, with increased miniature excitatory postsynaptic current frequency in networks but not in autapses, and synaptic failure during sustained high-frequency stimulation.

caveat_citations.title: Clinical overview of the seizure risk of dalfampridine.
caveat_citations.quote: Its mechanism of action and narrow therapeutic range suggest the need to evaluate the seizure risk in treated MS patients.

test.what_to_test: Sort STX1B variants into release-down and release-up classes in human iPSC-derived neurons (the network-excitability assay already published for G226R), then test 4-aminopyridine only on the release-down class.
test.existing_assay_note: The STX1B iPSC network assay exists (PMID:42673765) and the SNAP25 I67N study (PMID:40181518) is the template for using 4-AP as a readout in human neurons. No STX1B patient organisation or registry exists to find participants.
test.what_result_would_change_the_plan: If 4-AP rescues the release-down class and worsens the release-up class, this becomes an argument for functional classification before any drug, not for the drug.

evidence.title: Acetylcholinesterase inhibitors (e.g. pyridostigmine) is aimed at ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis.
Variants in SNAP25 cause SNAP25-related disorders. Curated databases record 2 clinical entities under this umbrella and definitive in ClinGen.
Gene Ontology annotates SNAP25 to ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis (GO:0048791 or a more specific child term), evidence codes IEA.

counter_evidence.title: SNAP25 variant I67N: synaptic phenotypes, drug response and proteome changes in human neurons.
counter_evidence.quote: These phenotypes were distinct from those of human neurons differentiated from hiPSCs originating from a patient carrying the V48F variant, which displayed an increase in spontaneous release.

attrs.title: Cholinesterase inhibitors for the SNAP25 myasthenic presentation
attrs.weakest_link: the pathway chain and the phenotype split: the drug argument needs a neuromuscular junction, and whether SNAP25-DEE patients have one has never been measured.

caveats.text: SNAP25 mostly causes a central epileptic encephalopathy; the cholinergic argument only applies to the myasthenic presentation (CMS18).

Cholinesterase inhibitors prolong the action of each released packet; they do not fix a presynaptic release defect, and in presynaptic CMS they are usually combined with a release-boosting drug rather than used alone.
One SNAP25 variant is strongly dominant-negative and another increases spontaneous release, so the gene label does not predict who could benefit.

caveat_citations.title: Congenital myasthenic syndromes: current diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.
caveat_citations.quote: Most patients are eligible for drug therapy with esterase inhibitors, 3, 4-diaminopyridine, ephedrine, fluoxetine or quinidine, but the effect of these drugs differs depending on the underlying genetic defect.

caveat_citations.title: SNAP-25 disease variants affect synaptic transmission by destabilizing SNARE complexes within a multimeric SNARE ring.
caveat_citations.quote: I192N is strongly dominant negative in the presence of wild-type SNAP-25, leading to impaired survival and reduced synaptic release.

caveat_citations.title: SNAP25 variant I67N: synaptic phenotypes, drug response and proteome changes in human neurons.
caveat_citations.quote: These phenotypes were distinct from those of human neurons differentiated from hiPSCs originating from a patient carrying the V48F variant, which displayed an increase in spontaneous release.

test.what_to_test: In people with SNAP25 variants and any fatigable weakness, do repetitive nerve stimulation first; only those with a decrement are candidates for a supervised cholinesterase-inhibitor trial, with the SYT2 case series as the comparison.
test.existing_assay_note: The SYT2 biallelic series (PMID:32776697) is the closest precedent: three patients improved on a cholinesterase inhibitor. CMDIR and the RARE-X SNAP25 programme can find the patients.
test.what_result_would_change_the_plan: A decrement on repetitive nerve stimulation in SNAP25-DEE patients without a myasthenic diagnosis would turn this from a hypothesis into a clinical screening question (gap:snap25-cms-vs-dee).

The atlas computed this chain: the curated cluster 'Presynaptic neuromuscular-junction failure (drug-responsive)' already places UNC13A-related disorders and 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) in the same group, but only the other members of that cluster have a therapy edge (no mechanism edge connects this disease to the drug's target mechanism); and the graph has no developed_for edge and no study testing this therapy class in this disease. The weakest link is the pathway chain: UNC13A reaches the aminopyridines only through 'the gene participates in vesicle priming', which is a statement about the protein, not about the direction the drug should push a particular patient's synapse. evidence.title: 3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) is aimed at ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis.
3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) has been investigated for SYT2-related disorders (stage: clinical).
3,4-Diaminopyridine (amifampridine) is aimed at ca2+-triggered neurotransmitter exocytosis.
Published work links UNC13A-related disorders to loss of function. Recessive truncating loss of function with microcephaly and fatal myasthenia.

attrs.title: Aminopyridines for the UNC13A presynaptic myasthenic presentation
attrs.weakest_link: the pathway chain: UNC13A reaches the aminopyridines only through 'the gene participates in vesicle priming', which is a statement about the protein, not about the direction the drug should push a particular patient's synapse.

caveats.text: The release-boosting argument applies to the neuromuscular junction. Most UNC13A patients have a central neurodevelopmental syndrome, where the same drug lowers the seizure threshold.
Three mechanisms coexist in UNC13A, including gain of function; a drug that increases release is the wrong direction for the gain-of-function class.
The strongest UNC13A release-deficit evidence is one patient's in vitro microelectrode study plus worm and mouse neuron assays.
UNC13A is linked to vesicle priming in the graph, not to Ca2+-triggered exocytosis that the aminopyridines target, so the mechanism match is one step looser than for SNAP25 or SYT2.

caveat_citations.title: Clinical overview of the seizure risk of dalfampridine.
caveat_citations.quote: Its mechanism of action and narrow therapeutic range suggest the need to evaluate the seizure risk in treated MS patients.

caveat_citations.title: Pathogenic UNC13A variants cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome by impairing synaptic function.
caveat_citations.quote: Using assays with expression of UNC13A variants in mouse hippocampal neurons and in Caenorhabditis elegans, we identify three mechanisms of pathogenicity, including reduction in synaptic strength caused by reduced UNC13A protein expression, increased neurotransmission caused by UNC13A gain-of-function and impaired regulation of neurotransmission by second messenger signalling.

caveat_citations.title: Loss of MUNC13-1 function causes microcephaly, cortical hyperexcitability, and fatal myasthenia.
caveat_citations.quote: RESULTS: Neuromuscular transmission was severely compromised by marked depletion of the readily releasable pool of quanta, but the probability of quantal release was normal.

test.what_to_test: In a patient with biallelic truncating UNC13A and fatigable weakness, repetitive nerve stimulation before and after a single supervised 3,4-DAP dose, with the quantal content measured if a muscle biopsy is available; and in parallel the same readout in an UNC13A-null neuromuscular model.
test.existing_assay_note: CMDIR lists UNC13A in its gene list, so the patients are findable; NCT02562066 is the completed amifampridine CMS protocol whose design (MFM score plus up-titration) could be reused. PMID:27648472 is the microelectrode protocol.
test.what_result_would_change_the_plan: Post-tetanic facilitation plus clinical improvement would make UNC13A a candidate addition to the CMS eligibility list. No facilitation, or any seizure worsening, ends it.
